ratings_why.fun: The mid and late game grow well along two clear paths, holding Stamps or sending fish home, but Tiers 1-2 are thin and each homecoming leaves a 1/1 Fry in the front row.
ratings_why.distinct: Choosing who goes home by moving them to the front row, and fish passing their stats to whatever stands beside them, plays unlike any of today's tribes.

verdict_why: The chain of homecomings needs a rule so a Fry can't turn into a copy and come home again in the same End of Turn; the rest could settle.

points.text: Thumbprint Parr's Spawn gives Stamps, and the Home check runs again. So a Fry can reach Home 2 in the same chain and become a fresh Parr, and that Parr may already be ready to come home again. If Stamps carry over, with Fish-Pass Keeper and Little Jack Gravel this can loop forever, with the Bend-Wife firing each time. Say that the copy starts with 0 Stamps, or that each unit comes home at most once a turn.
Climbing from a weak start is hard when Stamps only come from surviving. Try the designer's own fix: one Stamp for each attack, and a second if it survived.
The 1/1 Fry stands in the front row for two fights, which costs tempo early. Giving the Fry Shield would let it survive and earn its Stamp, which fits the cycle.
The year-class rule is hard to track during recruiting. A simpler idea: Run units that share the most common Stamp count gain +1/+1, which keeps the reunion theme.
Pilgrim Guide gives 2 gold every few turns, which is a slow economy piece for Tier 2. It could also pay 1 gold when its Fry hatches, so the whole cycle pays.

standouts.why: A Tier 3 piece that names the hoard build, and its Start of Combat attack gives it tempo right away.
Spared twice and bigger each time she spawns: a growth arc you can plan three turns ahead.
A real capstone: it fires every Spawn on the board and resets instead of dying, so the spawning build is worth reaching.

weakest.why: Fiddly to read, and the payoff is small for the counting it asks.
Slow, small gold, and it leaves a Fry gap each time.
Comes home on turn 2 or 3 for a small buff and leaves a 1/1 in the front row: it costs more tempo than it gives.

flags.note: Fry hatching inside a homecoming chain can make an unbounded loop with Parr, Fish-Pass Keeper and Jack Gravel, unless the copy's Stamps reset.
Not said: whether a fresh copy hatched from a Fry keeps the Fry's Stamps, and so whether it can come home again at once.
Stamps never reset in the back row, so the total grows each turn and Llyn Llyw's in-fight Attack grows faster than linearly late in a game.
A Kelt copy plus the Fry's copy for each spent fish makes triples very fast.
A golden Jack beside Bradán repeats every Spawn on the board, including Pilgrim Guide's gold.
+2/+2 to all Run units for every spawn grows with chain length, so it runs very hot in a long chain.
